81. Threading and Concurrency in Data Processing数据处理中的线程与并发

Matthew Housley, PhD

马修·豪斯利 博士

In a typical modern environment, data flows through complex distributed systems at each stage of a data pipeline, and servers must reliably maintain numerous connections to their peers. The Amazon Kinesis outage in late 2020 illustrates the consequences of ignoring concurrency problems. The outage, which occurred on November 25, took down a large swath of the internet. In this discussion, I'll assume that you've read Amazon's official report. The report uncovers several engineering blunders, but we will focus primarily on the limits of thread-based concurrency.

在典型现代环境中，数据在数据管道的每个阶段流经复杂的分布式系统，服务器必须可靠地维护与对等节点的众多连接。2020 年末 Amazon Kinesis 宕机事件，展示了忽视并发问题的后果。这次 11 月 25 日发生的宕机，搞瘫了一大片互联网。在讨论中，我假设你已经读过 Amazon 的官方报告。报告揭示了几个工程失误，但我们主要关注基于线程的并发的局限。

Operating System Threading操作系统线程

In Linux and most other modern operating systems, threads are a mechanism for allowing a CPU to execute a number of concurrent tasks far exceeding the number of available CPU cores. A thread gets access to a CPU core during an allotted time; when time runs out, thread state is dumped to system memory, and the next thread is loaded into the core. Rapid cycling allows the operating system to maintain the illusion that all threads are running simultaneously. Threads provide an easy mechanism for managing many network connections.

在 Linux 和大多数其他现代操作系统中，线程是一种机制，让 CPU 能执行远超可用 CPU 核数的并发任务。一个线程在分配的时间片内获得 CPU 核访问权；时间到了，线程状态被转储到系统内存，下一个线程被加载进核。快速循环让操作系统维持所有线程同时运行的错觉。线程为管理大量网络连接提供了简单机制。

— p.189 —

Threading Overhead线程开销

The new capacity had caused all of the servers in the fleet to exceed the maximum number of threads allowed by an operating system configuration. Threads are expensive. Each thread maintains its own stack, so thousands of connections consume substantial system memory. Switching threads is slow, consuming on the order of a few microseconds of core time, and a large number of threads can drive a high rate of context switching. Linux imposes a thread limit to prevent systems from grinding to a halt because of thread overhead.

新扩容导致集群中所有服务器都超过了操作系统配置允许的最大线程数。线程是昂贵的。每个线程维护自己的栈，所以几千个连接会消耗大量系统内存。切换线程很慢，每次要花几微秒的核时间，大量线程会导致高频率的上下文切换。Linux 强加线程限制，以防止系统因线程开销而彻底卡死。

Solving the C10K Problem解决 C10K 问题

Fortunately, the engineering community overcame the concurrency limitations of threads years ago. Nginx—first released in 2004—was designed from the ground up to serve more than 10,000 simultaneous clients (C10K) by tasking each thread to manage many connections. The Go programming language builds software on concurrency primitives—goroutines—that are automatically multiplexed across a small number of threads optimized to available cores.

幸运的是，工程界多年前就克服了线程的并发限制。Nginx——2004 年首次发布——从头开始就是为服务超过 10000 个并发客户端（C10K）而设计的，做法是让每个线程管理许多连接。Go 语言基于并发原语——goroutine——构建软件，goroutine 自动复用在少量针对可用核优化的线程上。

Scaling Is Not a Magic Bullet扩展不是万能药

Cloud native engineers have internalized the idea that scaling and concurrency can solve any problem; tech companies now routinely spin up clusters consisting of thousands of instances, and single servers can manage over 10 million connections. However, the Kinesis outage reminds us that scaling is viable only when built on sound underlying concurrency engineering.

云原生工程师已经内化了“扩展和并发能解决任何问题”的想法；科技公司现在 routinely 起由几千实例组成的集群，单台服务器可以管理超过 1000 万连接。然而 Kinesis 宕机提醒我们：扩展只有建立在稳健的底层并发工程之上才可行。

82. Three Important Distributed Programming Concepts三个重要的分布式编程概念

Adi Polak

阿迪·波拉克

Many data engineers create pipelines for extract, transform, load (ETL) or extract, load, transform (ELT) operations. During a transform (T) task, you might be working with data that fits in one machine's memory. However, often the data will require you to use frameworks/solutions that leverage distributed parallel computation to achieve the desired goal. To support that, many researchers have developed models of distributed programming and computation embodied in known frameworks such as Apache Spark, Apache Cassandra, Apache Kafka, TensorFlow, and more. Let's look at the three most used distributed programming models for data analytics and distributed machine learning.

许多数据工程师为 ETL 或 ELT 操作创建管道。在转换（T）任务中，你可能处理的是单机内存放得下的数据。然而，数据常常需要你用利用分布式并行计算的框架/方案来达成目标。为此，许多研究者开发了分布式编程和计算模型，体现在 Apache Spark、Apache Cassandra、Apache Kafka、TensorFlow 等知名框架中。我们看一下数据分析和分布式机器学习最常用的三种分布式编程模型。

MapReduce AlgorithmMapReduce 算法

MapReduce is a distributed computation algorithm developed by Google in 2004. As developers, we specify a map function that processes a key/value pair to generate a set of intermediate key/value pairs, and a reduce function that merges all intermediate values associated with the same intermediate key. This approach is an extension of the split-apply-combine strategy for data analysis.

MapReduce 是 Google 于 2004 年开发的分布式计算算法。作为开发者，我们指定一个 map 函数处理键/值对、生成一组中间键/值对，以及一个 reduce 函数把同一中间键关联的所有中间值合并。这种方法是数据分析 split-apply-combine 策略的扩展。

In practice, every task is split into multiple map and reduce functions. Data is distributed over multiple nodes/machines, and each chunk of data is processed on a node. A logic function is applied to the data on that node, and later the reduce operation combines data via the shuffle mechanism. In this process, the nodes redistribute the data based on the map function key's output.

实践中，每个任务被拆成多个 map 和 reduce 函数。数据分布在多节点/多机器上，每个数据块在一个节点上处理。一个逻辑函数应用于该节点上的数据，然后 reduce 操作通过 shuffle 机制合并数据。在这个过程中，节点根据 map 函数键的输出重新分布数据。

Later, we can apply more logic to the combined data or go for another round of split-apply-combine if necessary. The open source solutions implementing these concepts are Apache Spark, Hadoop MapReduce, Apache Flink, and more.

之后我们可以对合并后的数据应用更多逻辑，或在必要时再做一轮 split-apply-combine。实现这些概念的开源方案有 Apache Spark、Hadoop MapReduce、Apache Flink 等。

— p.191 —

Distributed Shared Memory Model分布式共享内存模型

Shared memory models originated from operating systems like POSIX and Microsoft Windows, in which processes running on the same machine needed to communicate over a shared address space. Distributed shared memory models try to meet the same need. In a distributed environment, multiple nodes/users communicate over a network and need access to the same data from various machines.

共享内存模型源自 POSIX 和 Microsoft Windows 这类操作系统，其中同一机器上运行的进程需要通过共享地址空间通信。分布式共享内存模型试图满足同样的需求。在分布式环境中，多节点/用户通过网络通信，需要从不同机器访问同一份数据。

Today, there is no one partitioned global address space. However, in-memory databases provide an answer to that need by adhering to multiple data-consistency levels. This allows a distributed programming operation on the data, where processes can write and read. Available open source solutions providing in-memory database capabilities are Redis, Apache Ignite, Hazelcast In-Memory Data Grid (IMDG), and more.

今天，并没有一个分区的全局地址空间。然而，内存数据库通过支持多种数据一致性级别，回应了这个需求。这允许对数据进行分布式编程操作，进程可以读写。提供内存数据库能力的开源方案有 Redis、Apache Ignite、Hazelcast In-Memory Data Grid（IMDG）等。

Message Passing/Actors Model消息传递/Actor 模型

Actors are threads/objects that encapsulate state and behavior. They communicate exclusively by asynchronously exchanging messages that are placed into the recipient's mailbox, and allow for the flow of communications/messages without locks and blocks. Building a distributed computation system on top of this model thus has the benefit of avoiding locks.

Actor 是封装了状态和行为的线程/对象。它们只通过异步交换消息通信，消息被放进接收者的邮箱，允许通信/消息流在没有锁和阻塞的情况下流动。在这个模型之上构建分布式计算系统，就有了避免锁的好处。

When picking open source solutions for this, check for message guarantees. Can you guarantee that messages will be delivered at most once? At least once? Exactly once? This will influence your system's operations. Open source solutions that implement messaging are Apache Kafka, Apache Pulsar, and more.

为此选开源方案时，检查消息保证。你能保证消息最多投递一次？至少一次？恰好一次？这会影响你系统的运行。实现消息传递的开源方案有 Apache Kafka、Apache Pulsar 等。

Conclusions结论

Now that you are familiar with these concepts, you can start to understand the bigger picture of data architectures and where each of these concepts comes into play.

既然你已经熟悉了这些概念，就可以开始理解数据架构的大图、以及每个概念在哪里发挥作用。

— p.192 —

83. Time (Semantics) Won't Wait时间（语义）不等人

Marta Paes Moreira and Fabian Hueske

玛尔塔·派斯·莫雷拉、法比安·胡斯克

Data pipelines are evolving from storing continuously arriving data and processing it as bounded batches, to streaming approaches that continuously ingest and process unbounded streams of data. Usually, the goal is to reduce the latency between the time when data is received and when it is processed. An important difference between batch and stream processing is the notion of completeness. In batch processing, data is always considered complete (as defined by the input), but stream-processing applications need to reason about the completeness of their input when ingesting unbounded streams of data. For example, a common task is to compute aggregates for regular time intervals, like counting the number of click events per hour. When implementing such a stream-processing application, you need to decide when to start and stop counting (i.e., which count to increment for an event).

数据管道正在演进：从存储持续到达的数据、把它作为有界批处理来处理，演进为持续接入并处理无界数据流的流式方法。通常目标是减少数据接收与数据处理之间的延迟。批处理和流处理的一个重要区别是“完整性”概念。在批处理中，数据总是被认为是完整的（按输入定义），但流处理应用在接入无界数据流时需要对输入的完整性做推理。例如，一个常见任务是按固定时间间隔计算聚合，比如每小时点击事件数。实现这种流处理应用时，你需要决定什么时候开始和停止计数（即一个事件该让哪个计数加 1）。

The most straightforward approach is to count events based on the system time of the machine that runs the computation. This approach is commonly called processing time. While it is easy to implement, it has a bunch of undesirable properties, including these:

最直接的方法是按运行计算的机器的系统时间来计数。这种方法通常叫处理时间。虽然容易实现，但它有一堆不理想的特性，包括：

  • The results are nondeterministic and depend on several external factors, such as load of the processing machine, ingestion speed, and backpressure.
    结果是不确定的，取决于若干外部因素，如处理机器的负载、接入速度和背压。
  • Processing time does not consider events that arrive out of order, which is always the case in distributed environments.
    处理时间不考虑乱序到达的事件，而在分布式环境中这总是会发生。

An alternative to processing time is event time. With event time, each event has an attached timestamp. For our example of counting clicks per hour, each click event would have a timestamp specifying the time when the click happened, and the streaming application would use the timestamp of the event to decide which count to increment. Event time produces deterministic results and correctly handles out-of-order data.

处理时间的替代是事件时间。用事件时间时，每个事件都附带一个时间戳。在我们每小时点击计数的例子里，每个点击事件都会带一个指定点击发生时间的时间戳，流式应用会用事件的时间戳来决定让哪个计数加 1。事件时间产生确定的结果，并正确处理乱序数据。

— p.193 —

A good illustration of the difference between processing time and event time is the sequence of Star Wars movies: the year each movie was released corresponds to the processing time, and the actual chronological order of the action in the plots to the event time.

处理时间和事件时间差异的一个好例子是《星球大战》系列电影：每部电影上映年份对应处理时间，而剧情中事件实际的年代顺序对应事件时间。

However, the challenge of reasoning about input completeness is not magically resolved by events with attached timestamps. An event-time application needs a mechanism to track its progress in time. Many stream processors, including Google Cloud Dataflow, Apache Beam, and Apache Flink, leverage watermarks for that.

然而，给事件附上时间戳并不能神奇地解决输入完整性的推理挑战。事件时间应用需要一种机制来跟踪它在时间上的进度。许多流处理器——包括 Google Cloud Dataflow、Apache Beam、Apache Flink——都利用水印来做这件事。

A watermark is a metadata message that advances the time of the application. Operators use watermarks to decide up to which time computations can be performed. A cool property of watermarks is that they can be used to tweak the trade-off between latency and completeness. More-conservative watermarks lead to more-complete results with a higher latency, while tighter watermarks produce faster, yet possibly incomplete results.

水印是一条元数据消息，用来推进应用的时间。算子用水印来决定计算可以执行到哪个时间。水印一个很酷的特性是：它们可以用来调节延迟与完整性之间的权衡。更保守的水印带来更完整的结果、但延迟更高；更紧的水印产生更快、但可能不完整的结果。

In the end, there is no wrong or right in these semantic trade-offs for stream-processing applications. Just keep in mind that time really won't wait for your data. Unless you tell it to.

归根结底，对流处理应用来说，这些语义权衡没有对错。只要记住：时间真的不会等你的数据。除非你告诉它等。

— p.194 —

84. Tools Don't Matter, Patterns and Practices Do工具不重要，模式与实践才重要

Bas Geerdink

巴斯·海尔丁克

If you're taking a dive into the data-engineering world, it's easy to be overwhelmed by technical terms and frameworks. Most articles and books about big data start with extensive explanations about Apache Hadoop, Spark, and Kafka. Diving a bit further into the sister-realms of software development and data science, the list of programming languages and tools becomes a never-ending pile of strange-sounding terms, of which you tell yourself, "I should investigate this!"

如果你一头扎进数据工程世界，很容易被技术术语和框架淹没。大多数关于大数据的文章和书都从长篇解释 Apache Hadoop、Spark、Kafka 开始。再往软件开发和数据科学这两个姊妹领域深入，编程语言和工具列表就成了一座没完没了的怪异术语山，你对自己说：“这个我该研究一下！”

I know plenty of engineers who keep track of lists of frameworks and tools that they have to dive into. However, that is not the way to go if you're just starting. Rather than learning the tools (frameworks, products, languages, engines), you should focus on the concepts (common patterns, best practices, techniques). If after studying you come across a new gimmick, doing some quick research should be enough to give you an idea of where to place it in the landscape.

我认识很多工程师，维护着一份要深入研究的框架和工具清单。然而如果你刚起步，这不是正确路径。你应该聚焦于概念（通用模式、最佳实践、技巧），而不是学工具（框架、产品、语言、引擎）。学完之后如果遇到一个新玩意儿，做一点快速研究就足以让你知道把它放在版图的哪里。

But all these abstract concepts can also feel academic and high level. The key is to find learning resources with good examples. Search for books, blogs, and articles that don't jump straight to the source code, but explain general concepts and architectures.

但所有这些抽象概念也可能感觉很学院派、很高层。关键是找带好例子的学习资源。找那些不直接跳到源代码、而是解释通用概念和架构的书、博客和文章。

When you come across an interesting piece of technology or a term that you're not familiar with, a trick is to always ask yourself the why question: Why must systems be distributed? Why is data governance needed? Why are there entire teams and products that are just doing ETL? Simply typing in these questions in a Google search or Quora will give excellent answers without the clutter of vendor/framework-specific details. After this, you can move to the how and what: How does this framework work? What use cases does it support? How does it interact with other technology? What are the costs of running this?

当你遇到一个有趣的技术或不熟悉的术语时，一个技巧是总是问自己 why：为什么系统必须是分布式的？为什么需要数据治理？为什么会有整支整支团队和产品只做 ETL？把这些问题直接输进 Google 搜索或 Quora，就会得到精彩答案，而没有厂商/框架特定细节的干扰。在这之后，你再转到 how 和 what：这个框架怎么工作？它支持哪些用例？它如何与其他技术交互？运行它的成本是什么？

— p.195 —

Here's some practical advice to help you on your way in the wonderful practice of data engineering. Pick a concept like data streaming, NoSQL, or functional programming that you're interested in, and do a quick internet search to learn the basics from documentation. Wikipedia is a great starting point. Then pick any tool that grabs your attention that is an example of the concept you're investigating (for example, Flink, Cassandra, or Scala). Block an afternoon for learning, spin up your terminal and favorite editor, and follow a set of tutorials. However, keep in mind when following along that you're learning a concept, and not the tool itself. Don't focus on details such as syntax and configuration too much, but rather keep asking yourself the why questions. Good luck!

下面是一些实用建议，帮你走上数据工程这门精彩实践之路。选一个你感兴趣的概念——比如数据流、NoSQL 或函数式编程——快速上网搜一下，从文档中学基础。维基百科是个好起点。然后挑一个吸引你、又是你在研究概念之范例的工具（例如 Flink、Cassandra 或 Scala）。腾出一个下午学习，打开终端和喜欢的编辑器，跟着一组教程做。然而跟随时要记住：你在学一个概念，不是工具本身。不要太关注语法和配置这类细节，而是不断问自己 why。祝好运！

— p.196 —

85. Total Opportunity Cost of Ownership总体拥有机会成本

Joe Reis

乔·赖斯

Choosing the right technology often comes down to cost—the time and money required. Total cost of ownership (TCO) is as ancient as enterprise software itself. While TCO has been a mainstay for decades, another cost is perhaps more onerous and far less discussed: total opportunity cost of ownership. As new technologies and paradigms come and go at an exponentially faster rate, companies need to keep their options open and take advantage of new and better ways of doing things.

选对技术往往归结为成本——所需的时间和金钱。总体拥有成本（TCO）和企业软件一样古老。虽然 TCO 已经是几十年的支柱，但另一种成本也许更沉重、却少得多被讨论：总体拥有机会成本。随着新技术和新范式以指数级速度来去，公司需要保持选择开放、利用新的更好的做事方式。

TCO consists of two big areas: the asset's purchase price and the continued operating cost over the lifetime of that asset. Companies may choose to purchase managed solutions, implement and manage an open source solution, or roll their own. Each of these decisions has its own trade-offs for both the long and short term.

TCO 包括两大块：资产购买价格、以及资产生命周期内的持续运营成本。公司可以选择购买托管方案、实现并管理开源方案、或自己造。每个决策在短期和长期都有自己的权衡。

Apart from TCO, there are two aspects to choosing a technology: the technology itself and the paradigm it represents. You can invest in technology X, which is part of paradigm Y. For example, on-premises Hadoop (technology X) in the early 2010s was part of the new big data movement (paradigm Y). If you heavily invested in on-premises Hadoop in 2010, you probably felt like this was a smart move.

除了 TCO，选技术有两个方面：技术本身和它代表的范式。你可以投资于技术 X，而它属于范式 Y。例如，2010 年代初的本地 Hadoop（技术 X）是新大数据运动（范式 Y）的一部分。如果你 2010 年重投本地 Hadoop，你大概觉得这是聪明之举。

Fast-forward to 2020, and the terms "on-premises" and "Hadoop" both seem antiquated. Since 2010, the world has moved into the cloud, and there are many excellent alternatives to Hadoop. Meanwhile, your data team dedicates significant time and bandwidth to supporting the existing system. You likely have little time or energy to consider replatforming to a modern solution.

快进到 2020 年，“本地”和“Hadoop”这两个词都显得过时了。自 2010 年以来，世界已经上云，有许多 Hadoop 的优秀替代。与此同时，你的数据团队把大量时间和带宽花在支持现有系统上。你大概没什么时间或精力考虑迁到现代方案。

Total opportunity cost of ownership (TOCO) is the cost of being captive to technology X and paradigm Y, while no longer benefiting from new technologies and platforms. It's the price you pay by going all in on technology X and paradigm Y, and not being able to make the transition to new paradigms. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos urges people to opt for decisions with "two-way doors," meaning you can reverse course or take another direction. Lowering your TOCO allows you to move fast, experiment, and introduce new technologies and paradigms that can greatly improve your business.

总体拥有机会成本（TOCO）是：被技术 X 和范式 Y 困住、不再从新技术和平台受益的代价。这是你全押技术 X 和范式 Y、无法向新范式转型所付出的价格。Amazon 创始人杰夫·贝索斯敦促人们选择“双向门”决策，意思是你可以回头或换方向。降低 TOCO 让你能快速行动、实验、引入能大幅改善业务的新技术和新范式。

— p.197 —

Here are some suggestions to lower your TOCO:

下面是一些降低 TOCO 的建议：

  • Avoid religious attachments to a particular technology or paradigm. Things change fast. As sure as the sun sets and rises, so will your favorite technology or paradigm eventually be obsolete.
    避免对某个技术或范式产生宗教式依恋。事情变化很快。就像太阳会落山升起一样，你最喜欢的技术或范式最终也会过时。
  • Separate computing and storage. Keep your data in object storage like Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.
    计算与存储分离。把数据放在 Amazon S3、Azure Blob Storage、Google Cloud Storage 这类对象存储里。
  • Use containers. This allows portability of your code between platforms and clouds.
    用容器。这让你的代码在平台和云之间可移植。
  • Focus on core competencies and avoid undifferentiated heavy lifting. Invest in managed services whenever possible. Free up your time to invest in things that move the needle for your organization.
    聚焦核心能力，避免无差异的重活。尽可能投资托管服务。把时间省下来投资于真正为组织产生影响的事情。
  • Keep learning. Always be on the lookout for better ways of doing things.
    持续学习。永远留意更好的做事方式。

Technology and paradigms change at light speed. Keep your options open.

技术和范式以光速变化。保持选择开放。

— p.198 —

86. Understanding the Ways Different Data Domains Solve Problems理解不同数据领域解决问题的方式

Matthew Seal

马修·西尔

Technology organizations commonly develop parallel tracks for multiple data concerns that need to operate in tandem. You often get a mix of teams that include data engineering, machine learning, and data infrastructure. However, these groups often have different design approaches, and struggle to understand the decisions and trade-offs made by their adjacent counterparts. For this reason, it's important for the teams to empathize with and understand the motives and pressures on one another to make for a successful data-driven company.

技术组织通常为多个需要协同运作的数据关切发展出平行轨道。你常常看到混编团队，包括数据工程、机器学习和数据基础设施。然而这些群体往往有不同的设计方法，并难以理解相邻同行所做的决策和权衡。因此，团队之间互相共情、理解彼此的动机和压力，对打造一家成功的数据驱动公司很重要。

I have found that a few driving modes of thought determine many initial assumptions across these three groups in particular, and that knowing these motives helps support or refute decisions being made. For example, data science and machine learning teams often introduce complexity to tooling that they develop to solve their problems. Most of the time, getting a more accurate, precise, or specific answer requires adding more data or more complexity to an existing process. For these teams, adding complexity is therefore often a reasonable trade-off to value. Data scientists also tend to be in an exploratory mode for end results, and focusing on optimizing the steps to get there only slows that exploration when most things tried aren't kept anyway.

我发现，尤其是在这三个群体中，一些驱动性思维模式决定了许多初始假设；了解这些动机有助于支持或反驳正在做的决策。例如，数据科学和机器学习团队常常在他们为解决问题而开发的工具中引入复杂度。大多数时候，要得到更准确、更精确、更特定的答案，需要在现有流程上加更多数据或更多复杂度。对这些团队，加复杂度因此常常是值得的合理权衡。数据科学家在追求最终结果时也倾向于探索模式，而聚焦优化到达那里的步骤只会减慢探索——反正试的大多数东西都不会留下。

For data infrastructure, the opposite is often the desired path for success. Complex systems have lower reliability and require higher maintenance burdens to keep operational. Choosing building blocks that are optimized for the end goal is usually necessary to reliably reach scaling targets under cost. Additionally, data infrastructure teams are often tasked with scaling staffing sublinearly to the size of the data and business needs. The result of this combination is that infrastructure teams are always battling the cost of direct attention on existing systems and finding time to redesign the highest-criticality systems with patterns that can continue to grow ahead of the data intake. The stark contrast here between these first two groups' modus operandi can lead to heated conversations about the best ways to solve shared problems.

对数据基础设施，成功路径往往相反。复杂系统可靠性更低、运维负担更高。为了在成本下可靠达到扩展目标，通常需要选择为最终目标优化的构建块。此外，数据基础设施团队常常被要求人员编制按亚线性速度随数据和业务需求规模扩展。这种组合的结果是：基础设施团队总是在与“直接关注现有系统的成本”作斗争，还要找时间用那些能持续跑在数据接入前面的模式，来重新设计最高关键性系统。前两个群体的运作方式形成鲜明对比，可能引发关于“解决共享问题最佳方式”的激烈对话。

— p.199 —

Finally, data engineers are usually tasked with precise and discrete tasks of producing tables of data. These usually have more well-defined outcomes and organizational requirements than their counterpart teams' problems. Tables need to be accurate, clean, and have a schema. Success depends on defining these contracts well for downstream consumers. Furthermore, they're usually under enormous time constraints to meet the demands of downstream teams. Thus, their solutions are usually focused on the immediate needs of a task and doing it as well as possible before moving on to the next. Designs for data-engineering workflows are usually aimed at solving a repeated task in a precise and efficient manner. Exactness and contracts are often more important than longer-term design for these problems. However, awareness of long-term problems is still a relevant and necessary concern that sometimes dictates designing a new pattern for a particular data problem before returning to the usual iteration cycle.

最后，数据工程师通常被分配精确而离散的产出数据表的任务。这些任务通常有比对应团队问题更明确定义的结果和组织要求。表需要准确、干净、有 schema。成功取决于为下游消费方把这些契约定义好。此外，他们通常承受巨大的时间压力以满足下游团队的需求。因此，他们的方案通常聚焦于任务的即时需求，在进入下一个任务之前尽可能把它做好。数据工程工作流的设计通常以精确高效地解决重复任务为目标。对这些问题，精确性和契约往往比长期设计更重要。然而，对长期问题的意识仍然是相关且必要的关切，有时会要求先为某个特定数据问题设计一个新模式，再回到通常的迭代周期。

What's important to take from this is not that one group's focus is better than another's, but rather that if you're in one of these groups, you should be aware of your own design bias. The success criteria of our data efforts on a day-to-day basis will influence how we look at adjacent problems. Sometimes leaning on another way of thinking for solutions can lead to a design that better tackles upcoming concerns, but it's also valuable to recognize when a mismatched focus is being applied to a problem.

重要的不是某一群体的焦点比另一群体好，而是：如果你身处其中一个群体，应该意识到自己的设计偏见。我们日常数据工作的成功标准会影响我们看待相邻问题的方式。有时借鉴另一种思维方式找解决方案，能带来更好应对未来关切的设计；但识别何时把不匹配的焦点用到问题上也很有价值。

— p.200 —

87. What Is a Data Engineer? Clue: We're Data Science Enablers什么是数据工程师？提示：我们是数据科学的使能者

Lewis Gavin

刘易斯·加文

The job title data engineer doesn't always come with the same sexy connotations as something like data scientist. Understandably, topics like machine learning and AI are always going to win the popularity contest. However, a good chunk of the work that sits behind these concepts stems from data engineering. I've seen a sea of articles recently talking about this exact point: that 80% of a data scientist's work is data preparation and cleansing.

数据工程师这个头衔并不总是带着像数据科学家那样的性感含义。可以理解，机器学习和 AI 这类话题总会赢得人气竞赛。然而，这些概念背后的一大块工作源于数据工程。我最近看到海量文章都在讲这一点：数据科学家 80% 的工作是数据准备和清洗。

AI and Machine Learning Models Require DataAI 和机器学习模型需要数据

Talk to any data scientist, and they'll tell you that obtaining data, especially from a source that has absolutely everything they require for their model, is a distant dream. This is where data engineers thrive.

和任何数据科学家聊聊，他们都会告诉你：拿到数据——尤其是从一个正好有他们模型所需一切的源拿到数据——是一个遥远的梦。这正是数据工程师发光发热的地方。

The benefit of a data engineer is just that: the engineering. A data engineer can not only provide you with data from disparate sources, but also do it in a way that's repeatable, current, and even in real time.

数据工程师的好处就在那个词上：工程。数据工程师不仅能从不同源给你提供数据，还能以可重复、最新、甚至实时的方式做到。

Clean Data == Better Model干净数据 == 更好模型

A 2016 survey states that 80% of data science work is data prep and that 75% of data scientists find this to be the most boring aspect of the job. Guess what—this is where the data engineer also thrives. They're great at joining, cleaning, manipulating, and aggregating data. All of this will be done in a repeatable way, providing a consistent source of fresh, clean data. This allows data scientists to spend more of their time on improving the model, and their morale will be higher as the boring part of their job has now disappeared.

2016 年一项调查显示：80% 的数据科学工作是数据准备，75% 的数据科学家觉得这是工作中最无聊的部分。你猜怎么着——这也是数据工程师发光发热的地方。他们擅长 join、清洗、操作和聚合数据。所有这些都以可重复的方式完成，提供一致的新鲜干净数据源。这让数据科学家能把更多时间花在改进模型上，而且他们的士气会更高，因为工作中无聊的那部分已经消失。

— p.201 —

Finally Building a Model终于开始建模型

The work of the data engineer doesn't stop here, as during the build, multiple iterations of the preceding steps will be cycled through. However, this section of the cycle is where the data scientist really shines, and I can't stress enough how important it is to let them do their thing here.

数据工程师的工作不止于此，因为在建模期间，前面这些步骤会被多次迭代循环。然而这个阶段是数据科学家真正闪光的地方，让他们在这里做自己的事有多重要，我再怎么强调都不为过。

Everything I've talked about so far isn't me trying to say that data engineers are better or worth more. It's to show that they can enable more-efficient workflows for data scientists that let them get down to the nitty-gritty.

我到目前为止说的一切，不是想说数据工程师更好或更有价值。而是想展示他们能为数据科学家实现更高效的工作流，让后者深入到最细的技术细节里。

A Model Is Useful Only If Someone Will Use It模型只有在有人用时才有用

The model will need to be implemented in a real-world application, and if you're worried that the model will become stale in a few months, don't be. A good data engineer will be able to work with the data scientists and translate their work into something that can be fed new data, rebuild the model, and automatically deploy it.

模型需要被实现到真实应用中；如果你担心模型几个月后会过时，别担心。一个好的数据工程师能和数据科学家合作，把他们的工作翻译成：能喂新数据、重建模型、并自动部署的东西。

So What Am I Getting At?所以我在说什么？

Data engineering is clearly an important field to consider. You can see just how much of the work behind building and deploying a data model can be accomplished by a data engineer.

数据工程显然是一个值得考虑的重要领域。你可以看到，构建和部署数据模型背后有多少工作可以由数据工程师完成。

The efficiencies gained mean that getting to the point of building the model will be quicker, and the resulting models will undoubtedly be better, as the data scientists have more time to spend tweaking and improving them.

获得的效率意味着：到达建模那一步会更快，而最终模型无疑会更好，因为数据科学家有更多时间花在调优和改进上。

— p.202 —

88. What Is a Data Mesh, and How Not to Mesh It Up什么是数据网格？以及如何别把它搞砸

Barr Moses and Lior Gavish

巴尔·摩西、利奥尔·加维什

We've seen how software engineering teams transitioned from monolithic applications to microservice architectures. The data mesh is, in many ways, the data platform version of microservices.

我们已经看到软件工程团队如何从单体应用过渡到微服务架构。数据网格在许多方面就是数据平台版的微服务。

As first defined by Zhamak Dehghani, the original architect of the term, a data mesh is a type of data-platform architecture that embraces the ubiquity of data in the enterprise by leveraging a domain-oriented, self-serve design. This idea borrows from Eric Evans's theory of domain-driven design, a flexible, scalable software development paradigm that matches the structure and language of your code with its corresponding business domain.

按这个术语的原创架构师 Zhamak Dehghani 的最初定义，数据网格是一种数据平台架构，它利用面向领域、自助服务的设计，拥抱企业中数据的无处不在。这个想法借鉴了 Eric Evans 的领域驱动设计理论——一种灵活、可扩展的软件开发范式，让你代码的结构和语言与对应业务领域相匹配。

Unlike traditional monolithic data infrastructures that handle the consumption, storage, transformation, and output of data in one central data lake, a data mesh supports distributed, domain-specific data consumers and views data as a product, with each domain handling its own data pipelines.

与传统单体数据基础设施在一个中央数据湖中处理数据的消费、存储、转换和输出不同，数据网格支持分布式、特定领域的数据消费方，把数据视为产品，每个领域自己处理自己的数据管道。

If you haven't already, we highly recommend reading Dehghani's groundbreaking article "How to Move Beyond a Monolithic Data Lake to a Distributed Data Mesh" or watching Max Schulte's tech talk on why Zalando transitioned to a data mesh. You will not regret it.

如果你还没读过，强烈推荐读 Dehghani 的开创性文章《如何从单体数据湖走向分布式数据网格》，或看 Max Schulte 关于 Zalando 为什么转向数据网格的技术分享。你不会后悔。

Why Use a Data Mesh?为什么用数据网格？

In 2021, the architecture du jour is a data lake with real-time data availability and stream processing, with the goal of ingesting, enriching, transforming, and serving data from a centralized data platform. For many organizations, this type of architecture falls short in a few ways:

2021 年，流行的架构是带实时数据可用性和流处理的数据湖，目标是从集中式数据平台接入、富化、转换和提供数据。对许多组织，这种架构在几方面不够用：

  • A central ETL pipeline gives teams less control over increasing volumes of data.
    中央 ETL 管道让团队对不断增长的数据量控制力更弱。
  • As every company becomes a data company, different data use cases require different types of transformations, putting a heavy load on the central platform.
    随着每家公司都变成数据公司，不同数据用例需要不同类型的转换，给中央平台带来沉重负载。

Such data lakes lead to disconnected data producers, impatient data consumers, and worst of all, a backlogged data team struggling to keep pace with the demands of the business.

这种数据湖导致数据生产方彼此脱节、数据消费方不耐烦，最糟的是：数据团队积压、难以跟上业务需求。

— p.203 —

Instead, domain-oriented data architectures, like data meshes, give teams the best of both worlds: a centralized database (or a distributed data lake) with domains (or business areas) responsible for handling their own pipelines.

相反，像数据网格这样的面向领域数据架构，给团队两全其美：一个集中式数据库（或分布式数据湖），由各领域（或业务领域）负责处理自己的管道。

The Final Link: Observability最后一环：可观测性

The vast potential of using a data mesh architecture is simultaneously exciting and intimidating for many in the data industry. In fact, some of our customers worry that the unforeseen autonomy and democratization of a data mesh introduces new risks related to data discovery and health, as well as data management.

使用数据网格架构的巨大潜力，对数据行业许多人来说既令人兴奋又令人畏惧。事实上，我们的一些客户担心：数据网格带来的不可预见的自治和民主化，会引入与数据发现、数据健康、以及数据管理相关的新风险。

Given the relative novelty of data meshes, this is a fair concern, but we encourage inquiring minds to read the fine print. Instead of introducing these risks, a data mesh actually mandates scalable, self-serve observability in your data.

鉴于数据网格相对新颖，这是合理的担忧，但我们鼓励好奇者读小字条款。数据网格非但不引入这些风险，实际上还要求你的数据具备可扩展、自助式的可观测性。

In fact, domains cannot truly own their data if they don't have observability. According to Zhamak, such self-serve capabilities inherent to any good data mesh include the following:

事实上，如果没有可观测性，领域无法真正拥有自己的数据。按 Zhamak 的说法，任何好的数据网格都内在具备的自助能力包括：

  • Encryption for data at rest and in motion
    静态和动态数据加密
  • Data product versioning
    数据产品版本管理
  • Data product schemas
    数据产品 schema
  • Data product discovery, catalog registration, and publishing
    数据产品发现、目录注册和发布
  • Data governance and standardization
    数据治理和标准化
  • Data production lineage
    数据生产血缘
  • Data product monitoring, alerting, and logging
    数据产品监控、告警和日志
  • Data product quality metrics
    数据产品质量指标

When packaged together, these functionalities and standardizations provide a robust layer of visibility into your pipelines.

打包在一起时，这些功能和标准化提供了一个对管道的健壮可见层。

— p.204 —

89. What Is Big Data?什么是大数据？

Ami Levin

阿米·莱文

You've heard the term big data numerous times.¹ Articles and books have been written about it. You might be using a product that claims to be such. Perhaps you even have it on your resume. But have you ever stopped to think about what it really means?

你已经无数次听到“大数据”这个词。¹ 关于它的文章和书已经写了一堆。你可能正在用一个声称自己是大数据的产品。也许你简历上都写了它。但你有没有停下来想过它到底是什么意思？

Big data has no standard, clear, agreed-upon definition. Some use it to describe data volumes, others as an indicator of data velocity, or of data of a large variety. None of these have any quantitative metrics that can classify a dataset as being big or small. Many use it to refer to specific technologies such as Hadoop, while others use it to describe data from specific sources such as social media or IoT devices, or so called unstructured data.

大数据没有标准、清晰、公认的定义。有人用它描述数据量，有人用作数据速度的指标，或数据多样性的指标。这些都没有任何量化指标能把一个数据集分类为大或小。许多人用它指 Hadoop 这类特定技术，而另一些人用它描述来自社交媒体或 IoT 设备这类特定源的数据，或所谓的非结构化数据。

So many conflicting, vague, and ambiguous definitions for big data exist, but none clearly describe the data or its use. Anyone can claim their products, services, technologies, or datasets to be "big data," and this claim can't be refuted.

大数据存在那么多相互冲突、模糊、暧昧的定义，但没有一个清楚描述数据或其使用。任何人都可以声称自己的产品、服务、技术或数据集是“大数据”，而这个说法无法被反驳。

The truth is that there is no such thing as big data. Large-volume, high-speed, varying-source data has always challenged our ability to derive value from it. Nothing fundamental has changed in the last decade to warrant a new term.

真相是：大数据这种东西并不存在。大量、高速、多源的数据一直挑战我们从中提取价值的能力。过去十年没有任何根本变化需要一个新术语。

Data management has always been about applying analytical methods to gain insights that improve decision quality. Nothing more, nothing less. By now, you may be asking yourself why so many smart, honest, well-intentioned data practitioners believe that big data is a real thing.

数据管理一直是关于应用分析方法获得改善决策质量的洞见。不多不少。到现在你可能在问自己：为什么那么多聪明、诚实、善意的数据从业者相信大数据是真东西？

Big data is nothing but a rebranding of existing offerings contrived by marketing people to revive interest and boost sales, and it is not the first time this has happened and probably won't be the last. In Big Data at Work (Harvard Business Review Press), Thomas Davenport says, "It is a well-established phenomenon that vendors and consultants will take any new hot term and apply it to their existing offerings—and that has already happened in spades with big data."

大数据不过是营销人为重振兴趣、提振销售而对现有产品做的重新包装；这不是第一次发生，大概也不会是最后一次。在《Big Data at Work》（哈佛商业评论出版社）中，Thomas Davenport 说：“厂商和顾问会把任何新热词套到现有产品上，这是一个成熟现象——而这种事在大数据上已经大量发生。”

— p.205 —

To find the root cause, all you need to do is follow the money trail. Big data advocates that you must store everything and keep it forever. It convinces organizations that they must use the latest technologies or they will be left behind. I'm sure you see where this is going.

要找根因，你只需顺着钱迹走。大数据鼓吹你必须存储一切、永远保留。它说服组织：必须用最新技术，否则就会被落下。我相信你看出这是要去哪儿了。

Pursuing big data is a wild goose chase. It distracts organizations from what is really needed to uncover the value in data, encouraging them to invest in storage and the latest technologies instead of improving data quality and decision making—which can be achieved only with domain expertise, modeling skills, critical thinking, and communication. These require education, practice, and time. Unfortunately, those things are not as easy or sexy, nor as appealing, as the false promise of big data being the silver bullet that will solve all your data challenges.

追求大数据是一场徒劳的追逐。它把组织从“发现数据价值真正需要什么”上引开，鼓励他们投资存储和最新技术，而不是改善数据质量和决策——后者只能靠领域专长、建模技能、批判性思维和沟通来实现。这些需要教育、实践和时间。不幸的是，这些东西既不那么容易、也不那么性感、也不那么吸引人——不像大数据是能解决你所有数据挑战的银弹这种虚假承诺。

We must refocus our efforts and stop chasing the latest fad, which is what we have been doing over and over again for decades. Reliance on any new technology, or a rebranding of an old one, is bound to fail. In my 25 years in data management, I have yet to see a technology that could beat a bad design.

我们必须重新聚焦努力，停止追逐最新时尚——这是我们几十年来一遍又一遍在做的事。依赖任何新技术、或旧技术的重新包装，必然失败。在我 25 年数据管理生涯中，我还没见过一种技术能打败坏设计。

¹ This chapter was inspired by Stephen Few's book Big Data, Big Dupe (Analytics Press).

¹ 本章受 Stephen Few 的书《Big Data, Big Dupe》（Analytics Press）启发。

— p.206 —

90. What to Do When You Don't Get Any Credit当你没得到任何认可时该怎么办

Jesse Anderson

杰西·安德森

Let's face it. Data engineers often don't get any credit. The praise rains down on the data scientists, but no credit rains down on the data engineering desert.

面对现实吧。数据工程师常常得不到任何认可。赞美雨点般落在数据科学家身上，但数据工程这片沙漠里一滴雨也不下。

This isn't fair, and it's something I hear from data engineers consistently. Some are annoyed and disheartened by the lack of credit. Some are ready to quit because they see their careers going nowhere or fear they won't get a promotion.

这不公平，而且我不断从数据工程师那里听到这件事。有些人因为缺乏认可而恼怒、沮丧。有些人准备辞职，因为他们看到自己的职业毫无进展、或担心得不到晋升。

Let's start with a few harsh realities. The CxOs, VPs, and other business people don't really care that you're using the latest technology, have unit tests, or have a scalable system in place. They care about the business value created by the data. (They only sort of care about these details when something goes wrong.)

我们从几个残酷现实开始。CXO、VP 和其他业务人并不真正关心你用了最新技术、有单元测试、或有可扩展系统。他们关心数据创造的业务价值。（他们只在出问题时才稍微关心这些细节。）

You've probably heard that "data is the new gold." I agree with that statement. The issue is that data in and of itself is relatively worthless. Data becomes gold only after it is transformed into something that makes the business money or allows for a decision to be made.

你可能听过“数据是新石油”。我同意这句话。问题是数据本身相对没价值。数据只有在被转化为能让业务赚钱、或能让决策被做出的东西之后，才变成黄金。

If you think about the data value chain, the data engineering part usually doesn't create the business value—it facilitates the creation of business value. The data scientists and data analysts are the ones most commonly creating this business value. They're the ones who are front and center when some kind of analytic or insight is shown.

如果你想一下数据价值链，数据工程部分通常不创造业务价值——它促进业务价值的创造。数据科学家和数据分析师才是最常创造这种业务价值的人。他们是那种在展示某种分析或洞见时站在舞台中央的人。

So, how do you start to get credit in your organization for what you do? As data engineers, we think that management should be interested in the technologies the organization is using. They aren't. That just isn't going to change.

那么，你如何开始在组织里因为你做的事而获得认可？作为数据工程师，我们以为管理层应该对组织在用的技术感兴趣。他们不感兴趣。那就是不会改变。

Instead, we as data engineers need to start focusing on what the business people are interested in. We need to get in the habit of talking in language that they understand and care about. We need to explain that the analytics are possible only as a direct result of the data pipelines we've created. We need to start tooting our own horns. Maybe the data scientists will even start tooting horns for us too. Start getting better at speaking the business language—and the credit, raises, and promotions will rain down upon you.

相反，我们数据工程师需要开始聚焦业务人感兴趣的东西。我们需要养成用他们理解和关心的语言说话的习惯。我们需要解释：分析之所以可能，正是我们所建数据管道的直接结果。我们需要开始吹自己的号。也许数据科学家甚至也会开始为我们吹号。开始更擅长说业务语言吧——然后认可、加薪、晋升会雨点般落在你身上。
